newsitem.title: HONG KONG: Hong Kong stocks weak in morning, consolidate.
newsitem.headline: Hong Kong stocks weak in morning, consolidate.

text.p: Hong Kong stocks were weak in Wednesday morning trade, as the market continued its consolidation following its recent powerful rally to record levels.
The Hang Seng index was down 33.39 points at 12,411.27. Turnover was HK$1.52 billion after the first hour of trade.

"I think the market is in need of a correction. I don't think it is inconceivable to drop a few hundred points more, testing the 12,200 mark," said Kent Rossiter, institutional sales manager at Nikko Securities.
Analysts said the Hang Seng was likely to follow Wall Street in the near term. The Dow industrials fell 29.07 points overnight to 6,061.80.

Alex Tang, head of research at Yamaichi International, said he expected a trading range of 12,000 to 12,600 points in the near term. "I think once this overbought situation is corrected, then the market will resume its uptrend again," he said.
"I think funds are still quite committed to come to this market," Tang added.
The Hang Seng index has gained about 11.5 percent since the end of August.
Wednesday's decline hit across the board, with all blue chips sectors suffering a setback.
In the property sector, Cheung Kong was off HK$0.25 at HK$62.00 and Sun Hung Kai Properties declined HK$0.25 to HK$86.25. Henderson Land also fell HK$0.25 to HK$69.75.
In the banking sector, HSBC Holdings slipped HK$0.50 to HK$155.00. Utility China Light fell HK$0.20 to HK$36.50 and Hongkong & China Gas fell HK$0.15 to HK$13.35.
Shares in Shanghai Industrial rose HK$0.40 to HK$18.65. The company expects to complete plans for an asset injection by year end.
